title: Weave the wind
html_source:
Frank Delaney suggests the possibility of an interesting link with T.S. Eliot’s poem ‘Gerontion’ which was published in 1920:

Vacant shuttles
Weave the wind. I have no ghosts,
An old man in a draughty house
Under a windy knob.

He says it may be just a coincidence but – especially in light of Haines’s later comment – it is intriguing that the poem also has the line:

My house is a decayed house,
And the jew squats on the window sill
